ModMetaData.name: The Network
ModMetaData.author: aRed
ModMetaData.description:
The Network is a persistent contractor, intel and procurement ecosystem that runs quietly behind the normal game.
You tell the world what you are interested in. The world reacts.
PHASE 1 (early development build): Intel. - Build a powered comms console, open The Network, and choose a contact: a fixer, a faction or the Exchange. - Ask them about any item in your game, vanilla or modded. You never say how much you want; the world decides what exists. - Pay the contact's fee and wait. A search runs in rounds, and one search can turn up several leads over time. - Leads are reports, not guarantees. They can be accurate, partial, outdated, wrong, a trap, an understatement, or much more dangerous than promised. - Every lead points to a real place on the world map, generated by vanilla site machinery, but what is actually there may differ from what the contact reported, down to none of the item at all. - Take all of what you find, take part of it, or walk away. You never have to kill every defender. - The Network remembers what happened.
PHASE 2 (early development build): contractors and procurement. - About a hundred persistent contractors live behind the scenes: lone operators and outfits, each with its own history, doctrine, morale, equipment and people who can die. - Ask a Fixer for an exact item and an exact quantity. Real contractors decide whether they want the job, turn it down for reasons you can read, or quote their price. - Accept a quote and pay the deposit. The work happens off-map. It can succeed, come back short, run late, go badly wrong, or leave people missing. The deposit pays for the attempt; insurance softens a loss but never erases it. - A failure may leave a place worth investigating. Successful goods arrive by drop pod. - Hire them again later, and what happened before matters.
No Harmony. No dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save. Before removing it from a save, use "Prepare save for removal" in the mod settings.
Contractors in person, the contract board and the rest of the ecosystem arrive in later phases.
